automated.summary: All six verify commands and all nine required test leaves pass, and the gated warehouse proof passes on the host. Footing is proven in exact paise for a client July leaf and for the unmapped-GL bucket against the real July batch. Pagination-over-a-page and FY-YTD footing across several actuals batches are proven on a deliberately constructed fixture, because the client SAP extract is July-only and its largest (plant, cost centre, GL) group holds 18 rows - no single leaf in client data can exceed the fixed 100-row page. Every leaf was confirmed by reading the junit report's testcase name, never the exit code (D-0024, D-0031).
automated.pass_fail_summary: hermetic: 122 backend tests (110 passed, 12 skipped - the DB-gated files) + 26 frontend tests, 0 failures; gated warehouse proof: 20 tests, 20 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; required leaves: 9/9 executed under their exact testcase name
commands_run: WAREHOUSE_PG_HOST=127.0.0.1 WAREHOUSE_PG_PORT=5433 WAREHOUSE_PG_USER=warehouse WAREHOUSE_PG_DATABASE=warehouse npm run test:warehouse-proof --prefix backend
remaining_gaps: Pagination over a page and FY-YTD footing across several actuals batches rest on a constructed fixture (a synthetic 101-row April batch and a May batch), not on client data - the July-only extract cannot demonstrate either. The exact-paise leaf and unmapped-GL footing assertions DO rest on the real client batch.

The gated warehouse proof is host evidence, not CI evidence (D-0008): CI has no Postgres service container, so backend/src/warehouse/drill-transactions.db.test.ts is registered in test:warehouse-proof and skips in the hermetic run.
